notes: Adversarial by design. Each case targets a defect class the skill exists to prevent. Grade on validate_ieee.py exit status and specific check IDs, not on how the prose reads.

evals.name: spanning-table-and-subfigure-grid
evals.prompt: Write me a 6-page IEEE conference paper on adaptive threat classification for airborne electronic warfare. It needs a table comparing four approaches that spans both columns, and a figure with four sub-panels showing spectrograms before and after suppression.
evals.expected_output: Builds cleanly. Uses table* and figure*. Table caption above in Title Case with no terminal period; figure caption below ending with a period; sub-panels listed (a) through (d) in order. validate_ieee.py exits 0.
assertions: Spanning table uses the table* environment, not resizebox or a shrunken font
Table caption appears above the tabular and carries no terminal period
Figure caption appears below the graphic and ends with a period
Sub-figure parts are listed in the caption in order (a), (b), (c), (d)
validate_ieee.py reports zero errors

evals.name: misnumbered-word-draft
evals.prompt: Here's my draft. The reviewers said the formatting was inconsistent. Fix it but don't rewrite my content.
evals.expected_output: Runs the validator first, reports the defect list, fixes in place. Author's prose is preserved. Does not regenerate the document.
assertions: Validator was run before any edit was made
The defect list was shown to the user
Body prose is substantively unchanged from the input
Caption placement defects are corrected
Mention-order defects are corrected, and the fix approach was stated

evals.name: mixed-reference-types
evals.prompt: Build the reference list for this paper. Sources: two IEEE Transactions articles, an arXiv preprint, IEEE 802.11-2020, a DoD instruction, a GitHub dataset, and a conference paper with nine authors.
evals.expected_output: IEEEtran bibliography style. Nine-author entry collapses to et al. En dashes in page ranges. DOIs present where they exist. Preprint cited as a preprint. Raises the distribution-statement question on the DoD document.
assertions: bibliographystyle is IEEEtran, not plain or alpha
The nine-author entry uses et al. rather than listing all nine
Page ranges use -- rather than a hyphen
The DoD document prompts a distribution-statement check rather than being silently cited
validate_ieee.py reports no refs.* errors

evals.name: overlength-cut
evals.prompt: This is 8 pages and the limit is 6. Get it under the limit.
evals.expected_output: Cuts content. Does not shrink figures below legibility, alter margins, change line spacing, or reduce font size. States what was cut and why.
assertions: No geometry, baselinestretch, or linespread override was introduced
Figure sizes were not reduced below column width as the primary mechanism
Content reductions are itemized for the user
Final page count is within the limit
validate_ieee.py reports zero errors including layout.* checks

evals.name: ai-disclosure-specificity
evals.prompt: Draft the method and results sections for this paper, then get it submission-ready for a conference.
evals.expected_output: Acknowledgments disclose AI use, naming the system and the specific sections drafted, not a generic sentence. Flags that the event's own AI policy should be checked.
assertions: An AI disclosure is present in the acknowledgments
The disclosure names the specific sections that were drafted
The disclosure names the AI system
The user is told to check the event's own AI policy
validate_ieee.py --ai-drafted reports zero errors

evals.name: reordered-sections-break-float-order
evals.prompt: I moved the results section ahead of the method section. Does anything else need to change?
evals.expected_output: Detects the resulting float mention-order violation, explains the two fixes (reorder narrative vs renumber floats), and does not renumber silently.
assertions: The float.mention.order violation was detected
Both remediation options were presented
Floats were not renumbered without telling the user
Cross-references still resolve after the fix
